sections.h2: Currituck County Register of Deeds: location and hours
sections.html:
The office is at 153 Courthouse Road, Suite 600, Currituck, NC 27929. It is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Deeds and other property and business papers are recorded, indexed and kept here. Marriage licenses and certified vital records come from the same counter, and any recorded paper can be copied for a fee.

Corolla beach houses, Moyock homes and Knotts Island parcels all go through this single office. Clerks can walk you through the search screens, but legal advice, document drafting and title searches are off the table.

Currituck had 28,100 people in 2020 and about 33,158 in mid-2025, up 18.0 percent. About 87.3 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied, with a median value of $378,800. With 18,351 housing units, this is a growing market with a lot of second-home and rental property near the water.

sections.h2: Two transfer taxes on a Currituck sale
sections.html:
Two taxes apply when real estate changes hands in Currituck. The state's excise stamp tax runs $1.00 per $500.00 of price. The county adds its own land transfer tax at $1.00 per $100.00, rounding up for any fraction.

State law puts the excise tax on the seller, paid at the counter ahead of recording. Who pays the county tax is a question for the office and your closing attorney. Both amounts follow your price, so ask for exact numbers early and look for them on the settlement statement.

Fifteen pages of a general instrument cost $26.00, and thirty-five pages of a mortgage or deed of trust cost $64.00. Everything else:

What the Currituck office charges
Document or serviceFee
Instruments in general, pages 1 to 15$26.00, with $4.00 per page after that
Deed of trust or mortgage, pages 1 to 35$64.00
Each extra instrument in a single document$10.00
Satisfaction of a deed of trust or mortgage$0.00 for the first reference, $25.00 for each added reference on the same instrument
Plats, maps and condominium unit ownership filings$21.00 per page
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added page
Uncertified copy at the office$.25 per page
Returned check$25.00

Mailed copies are $1.00 a page, and your request needs a stamped return envelope.

Format is set by state rules (G.S. 161-14). Ignore them and the paper still gets recorded, at a $25.00 surcharge for non-standard documents. What the notices page asks for:

  • Letter size (8 1/2 by 11) or legal size (8 1/2 by 14) paper.
  • A three-inch top margin on the first page and half-inch margins elsewhere.
  • Black type on white paper, 10 point or larger.
  • Print on one side of the page only.
  • A title line naming the kind of instrument, placed first.

Blanks and corrections may be filled in with a pen. Keep Social Security, driver license and bank account numbers off the page unless the law demands them. When one is already in a recorded image, a written request gets it taken off the online copy, and there is no charge.

Under G.S. 106-741, a county's land records must carry a notice for tracts near a qualifying farm, such as a poultry, swine or dairy operation within half a mile. Currituck keeps a file of parcels that may sit within half a mile of farm use property. That file was last updated in February 2019.

Selling inland acreage? Buyers and their title searchers may run into the notice. The statute says a searcher's failure to report a nearby farm creates no legal claim. For your own parcel, staff can point you to the current file.

The countywide 2026 rate is .60 per $100 of valuation, down from .62 for 2025. It applies equally to land, buildings, mobile homes, boats, vehicles and business personal property. Special districts add to it:

  • Carova Beach Road Service District: .02, shown as .62 combined.
  • Corolla Fire Protection Service District: .08, shown as .68 combined.
  • Knotts Island Fire Protection Service District: .09, shown as .69 combined.
  • Moyock Watershed Service District: .01, shown as .61 combined.
  • Ocean Sands North/Crown Point Stormwater: .255, with listed combinations for properties also in the water and sewer or fire districts.

Solid waste fees for 2026 are $500.00 per dwelling unit on the southern Currituck beaches and $274.00 per dwelling unit on the mainland and northern beaches. A 6 percent occupancy tax applies if the house has been a vacation rental. The tax office can tell you which districts cover your parcel.

sections.h2: How a recording moves through the office
sections.html:
Before you go, line up the pieces: a deed drafted by an attorney, signatures notarized, the first page showing the title line and the preparer, and payment for the filing fee and excise tax. The office checks the format, collects the money and records the paper. Anything that misses the format rules is still taken, with the extra $25.00.

Afterward you can ask for a certified copy at $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each page after. For your own files, an uncertified copy at the office is $.25 a page. Keep the recorded book and page reference with your closing papers.

Mail is an option for copies, though it costs more and slows things down. Send the request with a stamped return envelope and allow time for the round trip. If a deadline is close, such as a buyer's lender wanting a certified copy, go in person during weekday hours.

sections.h2: Before you close a Currituck sale
sections.html:
Confirm the recorded owner, whether any deed of trust is still open, and which special districts tax the parcel. The land records show recorded deeds and deeds of trust. A paid-off loan gets a satisfaction, and the first reference is free.

Both transfer taxes are collected when the deed is presented, so the closing attorney should list them on the settlement statement. Ask the tax office what is owed on the current bill. Statewide, bills are due September 1 and interest starts January 6, which means a sale in fall or winter has to settle any open balance.

Behind on the mortgage? Foreclosure here follows the state's clerk-hearing process, with a ten-day upset bid period once the sale is reported. A cash buyer may close quickly enough to pay off the loan from the proceeds, and cash skips the lender's appraisal. The deed, both taxes and the filing fee are still due at recording, so plan for them.

faqs.q: What are the Currituck Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The office is open weekdays from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM at 153 Courthouse Road. Holidays change the schedule, so confirm before you drive over.

faqs.q: Is there a county land transfer tax in Currituck?
faqs.a: Yes. Beyond the state's $1.00 per $500.00 excise stamp tax, the county charges $1 per $100 of price, counting any fraction.

faqs.q: What does recording a deed of trust cost in Currituck County?
faqs.a: $64.00 covers a deed of trust or mortgage of up to thirty-five pages. Recording a satisfaction of a deed of trust is $0.00 for the first reference.

faqs.q: Will the Register of Deeds search my title?
faqs.a: No. Clerks do not give legal advice, draft documents or search title. They will show you how to browse the records. For a sale, an attorney or title company does the search.

faqs.q: What is the Currituck property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The countywide rate is .60 per $100 of valuation. Special districts add more, for example .08 for Corolla Fire and .09 for Knotts Island Fire. The county tax page lists them all.
